title: Reverse predicate-lock granularity to coarsest (0/0) after default restore was harmful
configuration_cause: Incumbent runs max_pred_locks_per_page=0 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=0 (coarsest SIRead granularity). r012 restored PostgreSQL defaults (2/-2) and was reject_harmful: TPS -8.1%/-10.0%, locks_total.p95 rose 330->2146, GetUserTweets p99 rose 493->1219us. The default restore increased predicate-lock bookkeeping; the coarsest setting is the better regime.
mechanism: r012 falsified the direction 'restore default granularity'. Per the adaptation policy, reverse with equal-or-larger safe amplitude: keep the coarsest SIRead granularity (page=0, relation=0) that the incumbent already holds, and additionally raise the per-transaction SIRead budget max_pred_locks_per_transaction 8192->16384 so promotion to coarser granularity is delayed further. Coarser SIRead locking plus a larger per-txn budget minimizes per-transaction predicate-lock churn on the dominant GetUserTweets read path, lowering locks_total and tail latency and freeing terminal capacity for TPS.
query_effect: GetUserTweets (87.6% of terminal capacity) keeps the coarsest SIRead granularity and a doubled per-txn SIRead budget, so predicate-lock promotion and bookkeeping per call stay minimal.
expected_tps_effect: Increase successful_transaction_tps versus incumbent by reducing predicate-lock bookkeeping on the dominant read path; r012 showed the opposite direction cost ~9% TPS.
expected_latency_effect: Decrease GetUserTweets p99 and locks_total.p95; lock_waiting_backends stays 0 (no lock waits observed).

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Keep coarsest page-level SIRead granularity at safe low bound 0 (allowed [0,256]); r012 proved raising toward default 2 is harmful.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: page-level predicate-lock granularity cap; 0 forces coarsest page-level SIRead locking

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Keep coarsest relation-level SIRead granularity at 0 (allowed [-2,4096]); r012 proved moving toward default -2 is harmful.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: relation-level predicate-lock granularity cap; 0 forces coarsest relation-level SIRead locking

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Double from 8192 to safe high bound 16384 (allowed [64,16384]); larger per-txn SIRead budget delays promotion to coarser granularity, complementing the coarsest page/relation caps.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: per-transaction SIRead lock budget governing promotion to coarser granularity

predictions.rationale: Coarsest page/relation caps plus doubled per-txn budget reduce predicate-lock bookkeeping versus incumbent; r012 showed default restore raised locks_total.p95 to ~2146.
Less predicate-lock churn on the dominant read path lowers its tail latency versus incumbent.
Freed terminal capacity from reduced lock bookkeeping raises completed-transaction TPS; r012's opposite direction lost ~9%.
No lock waits observed (max 0); coarser SIRead granularity should not introduce blocking waits.

alternatives.statement: If the TPS gain comes only from the larger per-txn SIRead budget, locks_total.p95 will fall while page/relation caps are irrelevant; a follow-up isolating max_pred_locks_per_transaction alone would confirm.
If GetUserTweets latency is WAL/commit-bound rather than lock-bound, locks_total.p95 will fall but TPS stays flat and wal_waiting_backends persists, pointing to the WAL commit-path bundle instead.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent already holds the coarsest granularity; adding the doubled per-txn SIRead budget further delays promotion. r012 demonstrated the reverse direction (default restore) is harmful by ~9% TPS, so this coherent coarsest+budget action should recover and exceed incumbent goodput.

nodes.label: Coarsest SIRead granularity plus larger per-txn budget minimizes predicate-lock promotion churn
